flow.costPlain: What each payment costs PayPal to run: $4,248M of transaction expense (card-network and processing fees) plus $386M of transaction and credit losses on its loans.

opex.note: Running the company: finance, legal, risk and offices.

follow100Note: More than half of every $100 is gone before PayPal's own staff are paid — that's the card networks' and processors' cut. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: PayPal doesn't print a gross-profit line; the split shown is its own 'transaction margin' math — revenue minus what each payment costs to process, and the credit losses on its lending.
oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges were $255M, up from $69M a year ago — the main reason net income fell 14% even as revenue grew. PayPal's non-GAAP figures exclude $178M of that restructuring plus $33M of intangible amortization, giving non-GAAP EPS of $1.45 vs the GAAP $1.25.
Marks on strategic investments and crypto assets were a $3M loss — immaterial this quarter, after years of swinging PayPal's GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was −$28M — interest and investment results roughly cancelled out.
pngFooterNote: The split shown is PayPal's own transaction-margin math.

segments.name: Transaction revenues
segments.note: The cut PayPal takes on every payment it processes — $487B of payment volume flowed through in the quarter, up 6%, across 6.8 billion transactions.

segments.name: Revenues from other value added services
segments.note: Interest on customer balances, partner fees and other services around the core payment — a shrinking slice as rates and mix shift.

takeaways.text: Total payment volume rose 6% to $487.1B and transactions rose 7% to 6.8 billion, with 440 million active accounts. The pipes are busier than ever — the question is how much PayPal keeps from each flow.
takeaways.title: The payment pipes keep growing

takeaways.text: Revenue grew just 2%: transaction revenues +3%, value-added services −2%. U.S. revenue rose 5% while international fell 2%. This turnaround is being run on margins and buybacks, not top-line growth.
takeaways.title: Growth is thin, and uneven

takeaways.text: PayPal returned $1.5B to shareholders via buybacks in the quarter ($6.0B over twelve months) and declared a $0.14 dividend. Management also raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to about $5.60.
takeaways.title: Shareholders are getting the cash

verdict: PayPal moved $487B of payments (+6%) but revenue grew only 2% to $8.6B, and a $255M restructuring bill helped cut net profit 14% to $1.1B — the turnaround story is now about discipline, not growth.
